course_metadata.title: Diploma in International Financial Reporting (DipIFR)
course_metadata.description: Comprehensive English curriculum and study reference for the ACCA Diploma in International Financial Reporting (DipIFR), covering Conceptual & Regulatory Frameworks, Sustainability Standards (IFRS S1 & S2), Accounting Standards (IAS/IFRS), Consolidation, and Exam-Style Practice.

syllabus_modules.title: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
syllabus_modules.section: Section A: The Conceptual and Regulatory Framework
syllabus_modules.summary: The theoretical constitution of international accounting issued by the IASB (revised 2018). Not an accounting standard and never overrides a specific IFRS/IAS standard.

key_concepts.definition: A present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events, having the potential to produce economic benefits.
A present obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result of past events.
The residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities.
Increases in assets, or decreases in liabilities, that result in increases in equity, other than those relating to contributions from holders of equity claims.
Decreases in assets, or increases in liabilities, that result in decreases in equity, other than those relating to distributions to holders of equity claims.

fundamental: Faithful Representation (Completeness, Neutrality, Free from Material Error, Substance over Form)

measurement_bases.description: Value at acquisition adjusted for depreciation/impairment.
Price received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction (IFRS 13).

measurement_bases.category: Current Value - Value in Use / Fulfilment Value
measurement_bases.description: Present value of future cash flows expected from continuing use or settling an obligation.
Cost of replacing an asset today with an equivalent asset.

syllabus_modules.title: Regulatory Framework, Sustainability & Ethics
syllabus_modules.section: Section A: The Conceptual and Regulatory Framework
syllabus_modules.summary: Institutional structure behind IFRS (IFRS Foundation, Trustees, Monitoring Board, IASB, ISSB, IFRIC), standard-setting due process, and the IESBA Code of Ethics.

key_concepts.definition: Integrity, Objectivity, Professional Competence and Due Care, Confidentiality, Professional Behaviour.
Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation.
Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations framework guiding escalation and public interest disclosure.

syllabus_modules.title: General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information
syllabus_modules.summary: Establishes the global baseline for disclosing sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably affect cash flows, access to finance, or cost of capital.

key_concepts.definition: Full range of interactions, resources, and relationships used to produce products/services from source to end user.
Mandatory linkage between sustainability disclosures and traditional financial statements.

syllabus_modules.title: Climate-related Disclosures
syllabus_modules.summary: Topic-specific application of IFRS S1 focused on climate risks (transition and physical) and greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1, 2, and 3.

key_concepts.definition: Direct GHG emissions from owned or controlled sources.
Indirect GHG emissions from purchased electricity, heat, or cooling.
All other indirect value-chain emissions (upstream and downstream).
Mandatory scenario analysis proportionate to the entity's circumstances.

syllabus_modules.title: Presentation of Financial Statements (Current until IFRS 18 Application)
syllabus_modules.summary: Sets overall requirements for general-purpose financial statements, structure, minimum line items, and current vs. non-current classification.

key_concepts.definition: Classification depends on rights with substance existing at the reporting date; post-year-end waivers are non-adjusting events (IAS 10).
Assessment covering at least 12 months from the reporting date.

syllabus_modules.title: Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements
syllabus_modules.summary: Replaces IAS 1, introducing five mandatory income statement categories, two required subtotals, and strict transparency rules for Management-defined Performance Measures (MPMs).
mandatory_subtotals: Profit before Financing and Income Taxes

key_concepts.definition: Management-defined Performance Measure: subtotal of income/expenses used in public communications outside financial statements, requiring full reconciliation with tax and NCI impacts.
Investing in assets or providing financing to customers, which shifts related returns/costs into the Operating category.

syllabus_modules.title: Basis of Preparation of Financial Statements (formerly Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors)
syllabus_modules.summary: Governs accounting policies, changes in estimates, prior-period errors, and incorporates fair presentation, going concern, and accrual basis transferred from IAS 1.

syllabus_modules.title: Inventories
syllabus_modules.summary: Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV) on an item-by-item basis. LIFO is strictly prohibited.

key_concepts.definition: Estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less estimated costs of completion and sale.
Specific Identification, FIFO, and Weighted Average Cost (LIFO prohibited).
Permitted when NRV recovers, strictly capped at original historical cost.

syllabus_modules.title: Events after the Reporting Period
syllabus_modules.summary: Distinguishes between adjusting events (evidence of conditions existing at reporting date) and non-adjusting events (conditions arising after reporting date) up to the date of authorisation for issue.

syllabus_modules.title: Related Party Disclosures
syllabus_modules.summary: Pure disclosure standard requiring transparency regarding related party relationships, transactions, outstanding balances, commitments, and Key Management Personnel (KMP) compensation.
